title: Random-ice 6-DOF load ensemble vs the IACS Polar Class design ice load (and the declared ISO 19906 pressure--area family)

hull.provenance: hull/main particulars and damping ratios are declared engineering inputs of this study; the radiation kernel is a synthetic passive model (see module docstring); MMG derivatives are declared estimates, not captive-model data

experiment.metric: per impact cluster: peak contact force (heave normal), peak contact area, peak contact pressure; plus per-seed maxima

entries.document: ISO 19906:2019 Petroleum and natural gas industries - Arctic offshore structures
entries.needed: Annex A, global ice pressure clause: the coefficients C_R and the area-law exponent ex together with the A_0 normalisation and the validity range in A
entries.reason: no licensed copy of ISO 19906 is reachable from this work tree and the standard is not public; writing a recalled coefficient would be fabrication
entries.consequence: the ISO 19906 comparison is run at TensorFEM's *declared* coefficients (C_R = 1.0 MPa, A_0 = 1 m2, ex = -0.28) and every ISO-19906-derived number is tagged non_normative; the exponent is swept so that no conclusion rests on that one value

entries.document: ISO 19906:2019 Annex A, local ice pressure clause/table
entries.needed: local (high-pressure-zone) pressure--area parameters and the local area definition
entries.reason: same as above: document not reachable, no transcription possible
entries.consequence: local pressure is not compared; only the global law family is used

entries.document: ISO 19906:2019 Annex A, pressure-area shape/correction factor clause
entries.needed: the shape factor clause that corrects pressure for non-circular or non-square contact areas
entries.reason: same as above: document not reachable
entries.consequence: the floe contact areas of this ensemble are rectangular (h x w), so a shape factor of order one is the expected correction, but it cannot be quantified from an anchored clause here

declared_values.source: tensorfem.iso19906_ice_6dof.ISO19906PressureArea defaults; declared engineering values of this study, not a transcription

code_pressure_area_exponent.caveat: at fixed AR and CFD; AR varies with the normal frame angle and CFD with the Polar Class, so the full trend in a design space is not a single power law

pressure_area_regression.note: slope of ln p on ln A over per-impact peaks; A is endogenous to the coupled dynamics, so this is not an independent measurement of the law (closure arm)

tail.assumption: iid per-impact peaks; the true peaks are clustered inside a floe field and the tail is therefore optimistic -- the comparison of the extrapolated 1/N quantile with the observed maximum is the check on that assumption

code_quantile.note: empirical_cdf = fraction of per-impact peaks below the code value; a value near 1.0 means the code brackets the whole ensemble

comparison_items.reference_label: IACS UR I2 I2.3.2.1(iii)(b) PC6 design force
comparison_items.note: the code is a prescribed glancing bow impact of a large floe; the ensemble is a random field of small floes, so the code/ensemble ratio is a scope ratio

comparison_items.quantity: median over seeds of the per-seed maximum peak force
comparison_items.reference_label: IACS UR I2 I2.3.2.1(iii)(b) PC6 design force
comparison_items.note: extreme statistic of the same ensemble, still not the code scenario

comparison_items.reference_label: IACS UR I2 I2.3.4(i) PC6 average patch pressure Pavg
comparison_items.note: no transport: the code's patch-average pressure compared with the ensemble's extremal local pressure; a small positive deviation would mean the code's average pressure is as high as the worst local peak seen in 24 random fields

comparison_items.reference_label: IACS UR I2 I2.3.4(i) PC6 Pavg
comparison_items.note: only 1 impacts (<5) with a peak contact area within a factor 2 of the code patch area 1.507 m2: the ensemble and the code do not overlap in area for this group, so no matched-area comparison exists

comparison_items.quantity: mean per-impact peak pressure vs the ISO law at the measured area
comparison_items.reference_label: ISO 19906 form p = C_R (A/A_0)^ex with DECLARED coefficients
comparison_items.note: the contact law of the simulation is this law, so a small deviation only proves the chain reproduces what it was fed; it says nothing about ISO 19906 itself

comparison_items.reference_label: declared ISO exponent ex = -0.28
comparison_items.note: same closure caveat: A is endogenous inside the law that generated it

comparison_items.quantity: fitted pressure--area exponent vs the exponent implied by the IACS clause chain
comparison_items.reference_label: IACS UR I2 I2.3.2.1(iii)(d)-(e) implied dlnP/dlnA = +0.282
comparison_items.note: the IACS chain carries no decreasing area law (its pressure rises with area at fixed AR); the code handles small areas through the Table 3 peak pressure factors instead, so a sign disagreement here is a formulation-scope statement, not an error

criteria.statement: >= 3 normative anchors, each with clause locator, verbatim quote and sha256
last 10 seeds agree with the full ensemble mean within 5%
per-item deviation vs the code with an explicit '<15%?' answer and a cause classification for every item

evidence.note: the 15% gate itself is reported separately in deviation_gate_15pct; it is NOT satisfied, and the cause is classified per item

criteria.statement: Weibull/Gumbel fit with goodness-of-fit and a stated tail assumption
answer 'is it < 15%' for every item and classify the cause

classification.formulation_scope: code and ensemble measure different physical quantities
classification.closure_tautology: the law is inside the simulation; agreement proves implementation only

honesty.closure_arms: items tagged closure_tautology compare the simulation against the law that generates its contact force; they can only prove the implementation, never the standard
honesty.iso_19906_withheld: no ISO 19906 number is transcribed; all ISO-derived values use declared coefficients and are non_normative
honesty.geometry_gate: no hull geometry file is used, so Cb/L/B are the declared ShipModel particulars and are not independently validated here
not_claimed: validation of the IACS design load against model tests
extrapolation of the 6-DOF chain to a real ship
